annotation.title_clean: We are all Individuals: The Role of Robot Personality and Human Traits in Trustworthy Interaction
annotation.title_en: We are all Individuals: The Role of Robot Personality and Human Traits in Trustworthy Interaction
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Lim, M.Y.; Lopes, J.D.A.; Robb, D.A.; Wilson, B.W.; Moujahid, M.; De Pellegrin, E.; et al.
annotation.summary_en: Mixed-methods HRI study of a social Robo-Barista showing extrovert/introvert personality can be portrayed through vocal and linguistic cues. An extrovert robot is preferred and trusted more regardless of user personality, and human traits such as propensity to trust and negative attitudes toward robots affect trust. No governance content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Extroversion/introversion can be accurately portrayed in a social robot via prosody and linguistic features.
Extrovert Robo-Barista preferred and trusted more regardless of the subject's personality.
Propensity to trust correlates positively, and negative attitudes to robots (NARS) negatively, with trust in the robot.
Individual attitudes and predispositions should be considered in HRI design alongside robot personality, role and context.
